title: Someone Was Impersonating Her in Online Affairs. She Says It Was Her Husband.

reading.body:
The summary describes a case of sustained online impersonation in which fake accounts were used to conduct sexual conversations, solicit money, and distribute explicit material in another person's name. This is identity theft carried out through digital platforms, not a failure of an AI system in the technical sense. Nothing in the available reporting establishes that AI tools were used to create the fake accounts, generate the fabricated video, or conduct the impersonations, though the existence of a fabricated sex video is consistent with synthetic-media techniques that are not attributed here to any specific method or tool.

The incident is relevant to AI harm catalogues primarily because fabricated or non-consensual intimate imagery increasingly involves AI-generated or AI-manipulated content, and the reporting mentions a fabricated sex video. Whether AI played any role in producing that video is not established by the single report summarised here.

What is not established is who created the fake accounts or the video, whether any AI system was involved in any part of the campaign, and whether the person Fernandes names as responsible has been charged with or found liable for any offence.

reports.title: Someone Was Impersonating Her in Online Affairs. She Says It Was Her Husband.

summary:
German actress and television personality Collien Fernandes discovered that someone had been impersonating her online for years, engaging in sexual conversations with men and sharing explicit material featuring her likeness. The impersonator had created fake accounts, conducted sexual affairs in her name, and charged money for promised access to her. After enduring this harassment since at least the mid-2010s and discovering a fabricated sex video in 2021, Fernandes decided to investigate the situation herself as a journalist rather than ignore the trolls.

Fernandes, who had recently finalized her divorce from German actor and comedian Christian Ulmen, had been a high-profile public figure known for her feminist advocacy and children's books about gender roles. During an evening in late March while filming a television series in Vietnam, she prepared to expose the person she believed was behind the impersonation campaign. Her investigation and eventual revelation sparked a feminist movement in Germany, bringing significant attention to the issue of online harassment and identity theft targeting women.
